title: PocketChat task contract
description: Three closed shapes: the policy an operator signed, the record a run leaves behind, and the summary a report prints. Every level refuses unknown fields, so a field this schema does not name cannot be read as a grant or as a fact.

tool_grant.description: read_file and write_file grant paths; memory_search bounds results. create_only is declared so that widening it is visible as a schema change rather than a value change.

items.description: Workspace-relative. No leading '/', no backslash, and the parser separately refuses empty, '.' and '..' segments.

create_only.description: The only write mode. A policy asking for false is refused by the parser.

policy.description: What a bounded task run is allowed to do, and under which budgets.

objective.description: The single sentence the task is trying to make true.

workspace_root.description: Directory inside the workspace the task works in; '.' is the workspace itself.

max_steps.description: Hard ceiling on recorded steps. A task that reaches it stops; it is never extended silently.

max_tool_calls.description: Tool calls across the whole task, including calls that fail. A refusal costs budget, because it consumed a decision.

max_context_chars.description: Character budget handed to the existing context compaction; the task layer does not implement a second one.

max_turn_tokens.description: Per-turn token budget enforced by the existing cost guardrail.

max_session_tokens.description: Whole-task token budget. Must be at least max_turn_tokens; absent means no session budget.

tools.description: Only these three tools exist. A tool not named here is not offered and not executable.

delegate.description: Finite serial delegation, off by default. Children cannot delegate; this is a batch, not an orchestration tree.

step.description: One recorded action. The summary reports these; it never invents one.

index.description: Order within the task, 1-based. Not a run id and not a request ordinal.

kind.description: model = one model turn; tool = one tool call; checkpoint = a recorded recovery boundary; recovery = a resume or rewind.

state.description: How this step ended, in the recorder's own words: running, completed, failed, refused, cancelled.

tool.description: Tool name for kind=tool, absent otherwise.

detail.description: Workspace-relative path or a one-line reason. Never a credential, never a message body.

run_id.description: The run that produced this step, when one exists. It is the link to the trace; the task record copies no trace fact.

checkpoint_id.description: Recovery boundary this step created or resumed from.

recorded.description: When the step was recorded, RFC 3339 UTC.

task_record.description: The one answer to 'where did this task stop'. Written once, appended to, never rewritten.

task_id.description: Also the record's filename stem, so it must stay a safe path segment.

policy_sha256.description: Digest of the canonical policy bytes. A resume whose policy digests differently is refused, because it would be a different task.

state.description: created/running/checkpointed/interrupted are active; completed/failed/cancelled are terminal and cannot restart.

terminal_reason.description: Why a terminal state was reached, as recorded. Absent means the record does not say; it is never inferred.
